answer: New identities start at zero, so an attacker must pay to build parallel histories across many wallets, and any detected collision burns the shale-hard collateral. Sybil resistance here uses a bonded stake plus a ridge-scored history: each agent must lock tokens and maintain a verified track record, where reputation accrues along a vine of attested interactions rather than raw account count. Cost scales with the number of fake identities, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
